standard_prerequisites: The functor classifying flatness in dimensions at least n, its sheaf property for the fppf topology, and the fact that it is a subfunctor of the corresponding functor with a larger bound
Purity of a module relative to the base, its preservation under quasi-finite base change and under etale localization, and the constructibility of the relative assassin
Etale descent for monomorphisms and for morphisms of finite presentation, the existence of a complete devissage in an etale neighbourhood, and the flat case of the statement
core_obligations: Use the sheaf property and the monomorphy of the structure morphism to reduce representability to the existence of one scheme with a surjective etale morphism to the functor
Descend to the case of a scheme base by choosing an etale covering and pulling the module back, and record that purity and the finiteness hypotheses survive
Record that a monomorphism of finite presentation is separated and quasi-finite, so that the question is local in the etale topology and, in particular, in the Zariski topology on the base

Assume the base affine, where boundedness of the fibre dimension makes the functor representable for large bounds, and run a descending induction on n: from the representability for n+1, base change to the resulting quasi-finite monomorphism and use preservation of purity to reduce to the case where the module is flat in dimensions at least n+1

In that case use the existence of a complete devissage in an etale neighbourhood to obtain finitely many etale morphisms covering the fibre and a quasi-compact open W containing their images, and use purity along the fibre to show that the set of points whose associated primes lie in W contains a neighbourhood of the given point

Use constructibility of the relative assassin and the constructible-containing-open lemma to shrink the base so that this set is everything, reduce to the disjoint union of the finitely many schemes, express the functor as a product of the corresponding functors, and conclude each factor by the flat case; the product then gives the required monomorphism of finite presentation

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce representability to one surjective etale cover using the sheaf property and monomorphy
Descend to a scheme base and record locality in the etale and Zariski topologies
Run the descending induction on n through quasi-finite base change and purity
Use a complete devissage, purity along the fibre and constructibility to shrink to a quasi-compact open cover
Reduce to a product of the finitely many factors and quote the flat case

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's theorem at source lines 2195-2203, the main representability result of the chapter: for a morphism of finite presentation and a pure module of finite presentation, the functor classifying the points where the module is flat in dimensions at least n is an algebraic space and a monomorphism of finite presentation over the base. The 104-line proof (2205-2308) is a genuine research-level argument rather than a routine reduction: it first uses the sheaf property and the monomorphy to reduce representability to producing one surjective etale cover, then descends to schemes and uses the local nature of the question in the etale topology; after that it runs a descending induction on n, in which the induction hypothesis gives a quasi-finite base change to which purity is preserved, reducing to the case where the module is flat in dimensions at least n+1; finally it uses the existence of a complete devissage in an etale neighbourhood to shrink to a quasi-compact open W, proves that the set of points whose associated primes lie in W is constructible and contains a neighbourhood of the given point (via purity along the fibre and constructibility of the relative assassin), reduces to a finite disjoint union of the W_j, and quotes the flat case. Neither the induction nor the constructibility step is recorded in the statement.
